# OHFIS

> Free online tools that run entirely in your browser: PDF tools, text tools, CSV and spreadsheet tools, image tools, time and calendar tools, business calculators, IT and web helpers, notes and privacy tools, and team tools. Files and text are processed on the visitor's device and are never uploaded. No account, no watermark, no limits. Available in English, German, Polish and Czech.

## About

- Site: https://ohfis.com/
- Languages: English (/en/), German (/de/), Polish (/pl/), Czech (/cs/). Utility tool URLs use the same slug in every language, for example /en/case-converter/ and /de/case-converter/.
- Privacy: all processing happens in the browser using JavaScript, Canvas, Web Crypto and WebAssembly. There is no server that receives files.
- Operator: Andreas Dittes, Berlin, Germany. Contact: ohfis@dittes.info
- Sitemap: https://ohfis.com/sitemap.xml

## PDF tools

- [Merge PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/merge-pdf/): Merge PDF files into one document in seconds. Put them in the right order and download. Free, no upload and no sign-up.
- [Split PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/split-pdf/): Split a PDF into several files: every page on its own, by page range, or every few pages. Free, with no upload and no sign-up.
- [Extract PDF Pages](https://ohfis.com/en/extract-pdf-pages/): Select the pages you need and save them as a new PDF, or as separate files. Free, right in your browser, with no upload.
- [Delete PDF Pages](https://ohfis.com/en/delete-pdf-pages/): Remove pages from a PDF in a few clicks. Removed pages are really gone from the new file. Free, with no upload and no account.
- [Organize PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/organize-pdf/): Drag PDF pages into a new order, rotate them, add blank pages or remove what you do not need. Free, in your browser, with no upload.
- [Rotate PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/rotate-pdf/): Rotate one page or a whole PDF by 90 or 180 degrees and save it permanently. Free, with no upload. Forms and links stay intact.
- [Crop PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/crop-pdf/): Cut margins or unwanted areas from PDF pages by drawing the part to keep. On one page or all of them. Free, with no upload.
- [Compress PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/compress-pdf/): Reduce the file size of your PDF without losing text quality. Choose how strong to compress. Free, with no upload and no sign-up.
- [OCR PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/ocr-pdf/): Recognize the text in scanned PDFs so you can search and copy it. English, German, Polish and Czech. Runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded.
- [Flatten PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/flatten-pdf/): Turn fillable form fields and comments into fixed page content that can no longer be edited. Free, in your browser, with no upload.
- [PDF to Word](https://ohfis.com/en/pdf-to-word/): Convert PDF to an editable Word document in your browser. Keeps headings, paragraphs and styling. Free, and your file is never uploaded.
- [PDF to Excel](https://ohfis.com/en/pdf-to-excel/): Extract tables from a PDF into an Excel spreadsheet. Numbers become real numbers you can calculate with. Free, and nothing is uploaded.
- [PDF to JPG](https://ohfis.com/en/pdf-to-jpg/): Convert each page of a PDF to a JPG image in the resolution you choose. Free, right in your browser, with no upload.
- [PDF to PNG](https://ohfis.com/en/pdf-to-png/): Convert PDF pages to crisp PNG images in the resolution you choose. Ideal for text and diagrams. Free, with no upload.
- [PDF to Text](https://ohfis.com/en/pdf-to-text/): Extract all text from a PDF into a plain .txt file, with paragraphs put back together. Free, in your browser, with no upload.
- [JPG to PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/jpg-to-pdf/): Combine JPG photos into a single PDF. Choose page size, orientation and margins. Free, in your browser, with no upload.
- [PNG to PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/png-to-pdf/): Convert PNG screenshots and graphics into a single PDF, losslessly. Choose page size and margins. Free, and nothing is uploaded.
- [Edit PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/edit-pdf/): Add text, highlights, shapes, drawings and images to a PDF in your browser. Free, with no account and no upload.
- [Sign PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/sign-pdf/): Sign a PDF by drawing, typing or uploading your signature, then place it on the page. Free, with no account and no upload.
- [Fill PDF Form](https://ohfis.com/en/fill-pdf-form/): Fill in PDF forms in your browser and save them. Text fields, checkboxes and dropdowns. Free, and your answers are never uploaded.
- [Add Watermark](https://ohfis.com/en/add-watermark-to-pdf/): Stamp text like CONFIDENTIAL or DRAFT on every page of a PDF. Choose size, color, angle and opacity with a live preview. Free, with no upload.
- [Add Page Numbers](https://ohfis.com/en/add-page-numbers-to-pdf/): Add page numbers to a PDF. Choose position, format, size and first number, with a live preview. Free, in your browser, with no upload.
- [Protect PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/protect-pdf/): Encrypt a PDF with a password using AES-256 and control printing and copying. Free, and neither your file nor your password is uploaded.
- [Unlock PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/unlock-pdf/): Remove the password and restrictions from a PDF you can open. Free, and your file and password stay in your browser.
- [Redact PDF](https://ohfis.com/en/redact-pdf/): Permanently black out names, numbers and other sensitive information in a PDF. The content is really removed. Free, with no upload.
- [Edit PDF Metadata](https://ohfis.com/en/edit-pdf-metadata/): See and change a PDF's title, author and keywords, or remove all metadata in one click. Free, in your browser, with no upload.

## Text Tools

Clean, convert, count, compare and extract text. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/text-tools/

- [Zero-Width Character Remover](https://ohfis.com/en/zero-width-character-remover/): Find and delete invisible characters such as zero-width spaces and BOMs.
  Text copied from websites, PDFs, chat apps and AI tools often carries characters you cannot see: zero-width spaces (U+200B), byte order marks (U+FEFF), soft hyphens, no-break spaces and directional marks. They break string comparisons, make database lookups fail and cause "mystery" errors in code, CSV files and passwords.
  How to use: Paste the text that behaves strangely. Choose whether no-break spaces should become normal spaces and whether emoji joiners stay. Copy the cleaned text. The list underneath shows which hidden characters were removed.
- [Case Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/case-converter/): Switch text to UPPER, lower, Title, Sentence, camelCase, snake_case and more.
  Fix a headline typed in capitals, format a variable name for code or tidy a list of names. The converter handles 13 styles: UPPER, lower, Title Case, Sentence case, Capitalize Each Word, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, CONSTANT_CASE, kebab-case, dot.case, aLtErNaTiNg and iNVERSE.
  How to use: Paste or type your text. Pick the target style from the list. Copy the result. It updates live as you type.
- [Remove Duplicate Lines](https://ohfis.com/en/remove-duplicate-lines/): Delete repeated lines and see how often each one occurred.
  Clean a mailing list, a keyword export or a log file by keeping only the first occurrence of every line. Options let you ignore upper and lower case, trim stray spaces and drop empty lines, so "Apple", "apple " and "APPLE" can count as one entry.
  How to use: Paste your list, one item per line. Choose whether case and spaces should be ignored, and how to order the result. Copy the unique lines. Tick "Show how often" for counts.
- [List to Comma Separated Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/list-to-comma-separated/): Turn lines into comma, tab or quoted lists, arrays and SQL IN (…) lists.
  Paste a column from Excel and get "a, b, c" for an email field, a quoted array for code or a ready-made SQL IN list. The reverse works as well: split comma, semicolon, pipe, tab or space separated text back into one item per line.
  How to use: Paste your list and choose the input separator. Pick the output separator, quote style and wrapper. Copy the result into your email, code or query.
- [Extract Emails, Phones & URLs from Text](https://ohfis.com/en/regex-extractor/): Pull emails, phone numbers, UUIDs, IPs, dates and more out of raw text.
  Choose what you are looking for from a library of tested patterns (email addresses, URLs, phone numbers, UUIDs, IPv4 addresses, hex colours, hashtags, @mentions, dates, numbers and IBANs) and the tool lists every match. If you know regular expressions you can enter your own pattern.
  How to use: Paste your text, logs or HTML source. Pick what to find, or choose "custom" and type a regular expression. Copy the list of matches.
- [Text Diff Checker](https://ohfis.com/en/text-diff-checker/): Compare two texts side by side and see every added and removed word or line.
  Paste the original and the changed version of a contract clause, an article or a configuration file and see the differences highlighted. Compare line by line like a code review, word by word for prose, or character by character for small edits. You can ignore whitespace and case, and export the result as a unified patch.
  How to use: Paste the original text on the left and the changed text on the right. Choose line, word or character comparison and any ignore options. Read the highlighted differences, or copy and download them as a patch.
- [Table to Markdown Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/table-to-markdown/): Paste cells from Excel or CSV and get a clean Markdown or HTML table.
  Copy a range in Excel or Google Sheets, paste it here and get a GitHub-flavoured Markdown table with aligned columns, or an unstyled HTML table. It also reads CSV, semicolon, pipe and space-separated data and can re-format an existing ragged Markdown table.
  How to use: Copy cells from your spreadsheet and paste them in. Choose Markdown or HTML, alignment and whether the first row is a header. Copy the table into your README, wiki or CMS.
- [Character Counter](https://ohfis.com/en/character-counter/): Count characters, words and bytes against X, LinkedIn, Google Ads and SMS limits.
  Paste a post, ad or message and see the number of characters, characters without spaces, words, sentences, lines, bytes and visible symbols. Progress bars compare your length with the limits of X (Twitter), LinkedIn, Instagram, Google Ads headlines and descriptions, page titles and meta descriptions, YouTube and TikTok.
  How to use: Paste or type your text. Read the counts and watch the bars for each platform. Edit until every bar you care about is within its limit.
- [Speech Time Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/speech-time-calculator/): Estimate how long your speech or script takes at slow, natural and energetic pace.
  Paste your talk, toast or video script to see how long it takes to deliver. The calculator shows three tiers: slow (110 words per minute, for formal speeches and nervous speakers), natural (150, typical conversation and presentations) and energetic (180, fast, enthusiastic delivery). You can also enter your own pace.
  How to use: Paste your script. Optionally set your own speaking pace and the pause after each paragraph. Use the times to trim or extend the text to fit your slot.
- [Fake Data Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/dummy-data-generator/): Generate realistic names, emails and addresses for test data instead of Lorem Ipsum.
  Fill a prototype, a demo database or a mock-up with believable people, companies, addresses, phone numbers, dates and amounts instead of "Lorem ipsum". Choose the fields, the number of records (up to 1,000) and English or German style names, then copy the table or download CSV or JSON.
  How to use: Tick the fields you need and choose how many rows. Pick the name style and output format. Copy or download the data; press "Generate" for a fresh set.
- [Smart Quotes to Straight Quotes](https://ohfis.com/en/smart-quotes-to-ascii/): Replace curly quotes, dashes, ellipses and ligatures with plain ASCII.
  Word processors and AI chat tools replace straight quotes with curly ones and turn dashes and three dots into single special characters. Those look nice in a document but break code, JSON, shell commands, CSV files and old systems. This tool turns them back into the plain keyboard characters.
  How to use: Paste the text with curly quotes or special dashes. Choose which groups of characters to normalise. Copy the plain text into your code, config or spreadsheet.
- [Remove Line Breaks](https://ohfis.com/en/remove-line-breaks/): Join text copied from PDFs into flowing paragraphs and keep real paragraph breaks.
  Text copied from a PDF, an email or a terminal is broken into short lines at the width of the original page. Pasting it into a document produces ragged paragraphs. This tool removes the hard line breaks inside paragraphs while keeping the blank lines that separate real paragraphs and, optionally, bullet and numbered list items.
  How to use: Paste the text with the unwanted line breaks. Keep or drop paragraph breaks, hyphenation repair and list handling. Copy the flowing text.
- [Add Prefix or Suffix to Lines](https://ohfis.com/en/add-prefix-suffix-to-lines/): Add text, numbers or tags before or after every line in one step.
  Wrap every line in quotes, add a bullet, append a semicolon or number a list: type what should go before and after each line and it is applied to thousands of lines at once. Use {n} anywhere in the prefix or suffix to insert a counter that can start at any number and be zero-padded.
  How to use: Paste your lines. Enter the text to add before and after, using {n} for a counter if you need one. Copy the result.
- [Sort Lines Alphabetically](https://ohfis.com/en/sort-lines/): Sort lists A–Z, Z–A, by length or naturally (v2 before v10).
  Sort names, file names, version numbers or any list. Choose alphabetical order, natural sorting (so "file2" comes before "file10"), sorting by line length, or by the number found in each line, and reverse the order if needed.
  How to use: Paste your list, one entry per line. Choose the sort type and whether to reverse it. Copy the sorted list.
- [Email Extractor](https://ohfis.com/en/email-extractor/): Pull every email address out of any text, remove duplicates and group by domain.
  Paste a mailbox export, a web page source, a CC line or any messy text and get a clean, alphabetical list of the email addresses in it. Duplicates are removed, addresses are lower-cased, and you can group them by domain to see which companies appear most.
  How to use: Paste your text. Optionally tick "Group by domain". Copy the list or download it as a text file.
- [URL Extractor & Tracking Parameter Remover](https://ohfis.com/en/url-extractor-tracking-remover/): List the links in a text and strip utm_*, fbclid and other tracking tags.
  Shared links are often full of tracking tags such as utm_source, fbclid, gclid or mc_eid. They make links long and tell the sender who clicked. Paste a link or a whole text and get clean URLs with the tracking parameters removed, or the text back with its links cleaned in place.
  How to use: Paste a link or text containing links. Choose a list of clean URLs or the full text with cleaned links. Copy the result. The summary shows which parameters were removed.
- [URL Slug Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/slug-generator/): Turn titles into clean, accent-free, SEO-friendly URL slugs.
  A good slug is short, readable and uses only letters, numbers and hyphens. Paste one title per line and get slugs for your blog, shop or CMS. Accents are removed (crème → creme), German ß becomes ss, and symbols and punctuation turn into single hyphens.
  How to use: Paste your titles, one per line. Choose the separator, case, stop-word removal and maximum length. Copy the slugs.
- [ROT13 Encoder & Decoder](https://ohfis.com/en/rot13-encoder/): Encode or decode ROT13 and other Caesar ciphers.
  ROT13 replaces every letter with the one 13 places further along the alphabet. Because the alphabet has 26 letters, applying it twice returns the original text, so the same button encodes and decodes. It is used for spoiler warnings and light obfuscation, not for security.
  How to use: Type or paste the text. Leave the shift at 13 for ROT13, or choose another shift. Copy the result. To decode ROT13, run it again.
- [Emoji Remover](https://ohfis.com/en/emoji-remover/): Strip emoji and pictograms from text, or reduce everything to plain ASCII.
  Remove emoji from comments, product descriptions, chat exports or data feeds before importing them into systems that cannot store them. Skin-tone modifiers, flags, keycaps and multi-part emoji such as families are removed completely, with no stray joiner characters left behind.
  How to use: Paste the text containing emoji. Optionally enable plain ASCII mode or choose a replacement. Copy the clean text. The counter shows how many characters were removed.
- [NATO Phonetic Alphabet Translator](https://ohfis.com/en/nato-phonetic-alphabet/): Spell names, codes and serial numbers in Alfa, Bravo, Charlie…
  When you read a licence key, booking reference or surname over the phone, "B" and "D" are easy to confuse. The NATO phonetic alphabet gives every letter a distinct word. Type any text and get the spelled-out version, with digits as words and spaces shown as a slash.
  How to use: Type the text, code or name you need to spell. Decide whether lower-case letters should be shown in lower case. Read it out or copy it into a message.
- [Random Line Shuffler](https://ohfis.com/en/shuffle-lines/): Shuffle a list into random order with a fair Fisher-Yates shuffle.
  Randomise a list of names for a presentation order, shuffle quiz questions or mix a playlist. Paste one item per line and press "Shuffle again" as often as you like.
  How to use: Paste your list, one item per line. Read the shuffled order. Press "Shuffle again" for a new order, then copy it.
- [Filter Lines (Text Grep)](https://ohfis.com/en/filter-lines/): Keep or drop the lines that contain, start or end with a search term.
  Reduce a log file, a keyword list or an export to just the lines you care about. Type a search term and keep the lines that contain it, start with it, end with it or equal it, or invert the filter to delete those lines instead.
  How to use: Paste your lines. Enter the search term and choose how it should match. Optionally invert the filter, then copy the remaining lines.
- [Merge Two Lists into Columns](https://ohfis.com/en/merge-columns/): Paste two lists and join them side by side, ready for Excel.
  Combine a column of names with a column of emails, or two exports that belong together, without a spreadsheet. Paste list A and list B, choose the separator and copy the aligned result. With a tab separator the result pastes straight into Excel or Google Sheets as two columns.
  How to use: Paste the first list on the left and the second on the right. Choose a separator such as Tab, comma or dash. Copy the merged lines.
- [Tabs to Spaces Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/tabs-to-spaces/): Normalise code indentation to 2, 4 or 8 spaces, or back to tabs.
  Mixed tabs and spaces make code and config files look broken when they move between editors. Convert leading tabs to spaces, or spaces back to tabs, with a tab width of 2, 3, 4 or 8, and strip trailing whitespace at the same time.
  How to use: Paste your code or text. Choose the direction and the number of spaces per tab. Copy the converted text.
- [Word Frequency Counter](https://ohfis.com/en/word-frequency-counter/): Rank the most used words and phrases, ignoring common stop words.
  See which words and phrases dominate an article, a transcript or survey answers. The table ranks single words, two-word phrases (bigrams) or three-word phrases (trigrams) with their count and keyword density, and ignores common stop words in English or German so that "the" and "and" do not crowd out the useful terms.
  How to use: Paste your text. Choose single words or phrases, and the stop-word language. Read the ranking or download it as CSV.
- [Text Splitter](https://ohfis.com/en/text-splitter/): Cut long text into chunks of a set length without breaking words.
  Break a long document into pieces that fit a limit: SMS or tweet threads, form fields, translation tools or AI prompts with a size cap. Set the maximum characters per chunk, an optional overlap and whether to avoid cutting inside words or prefer paragraph boundaries. Each chunk can be copied separately or all together.
  How to use: Paste the long text. Set the maximum characters per chunk and the options. Copy single chunks or download them all.
- [Buzzword Detector](https://ohfis.com/en/buzzword-detector/): Highlight corporate jargon and see plain-language alternatives.
  "Let's circle back and leverage our core competencies." Paste an email, report or job post and the tool highlights over 50 overused business phrases, shows how many there are per 100 words and suggests a plain replacement for each one ("circle back" → "follow up").
  How to use: Paste your text. Read the highlighted phrases and the replacement table. Rewrite the passages that sound vague.
- [Indented Text to JSON, HTML & XML](https://ohfis.com/en/outline-converter/): Convert an indented outline into nested JSON, HTML lists, XML, Markdown or YAML.
  Write a tree the easy way (one item per line, indented to show hierarchy) and convert it to a structured format. Typical uses: a menu structure for a website, a folder tree, an org structure or a table of contents.
  How to use: Type or paste your outline, indenting children with tabs or spaces. Pick the output format. Copy the generated structure.
- [Text to Hex, Binary & Base32 Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/text-base-converter/): Convert text between hex, binary, decimal, octal, Base32 and Base64.
  See how a text is stored in bytes. Convert it to hexadecimal, binary, decimal, octal, Base32 or Base64 and back again. This is useful for debugging encodings, preparing test data or solving puzzles.
  How to use: Choose the input format and the output format. Paste the value. Copy the result.
- [Morse Code Translator](https://ohfis.com/en/morse-code-translator/): Translate text to Morse code and back, and play it as beeps.
  Type a message to get dots and dashes, or paste Morse code to read it. The direction is detected automatically. Press "Play as sound" to hear the message as beeps at the speed and pitch you choose.
  How to use: Type text or paste Morse code. Read the translation, or press "Play as sound". Adjust the speed and pitch to taste, then copy the result.

## Spreadsheet & CSV Tools

Fix, convert, merge, compare and reshape CSV and spreadsheet data. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/spreadsheet-csv-tools/

- [CSV Delimiter Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-delimiter-converter/): Detect the separator of a CSV and convert it to comma, semicolon, tab or pipe.
  Excel in Germany, France or Poland saves CSV files with semicolons, US tools expect commas, databases like tabs. If a file opens as one long column, the separator is wrong. This tool detects the delimiter of your file and rewrites it with the one you need, converting CSV to TSV and back without breaking cells that contain commas, quotes or line breaks.
  How to use: Paste your data or open a file. The detected separator is shown. Choose the output separator under "Output format". Copy the result or download it as a new file.
- [Large CSV File Viewer](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-viewer/): Open CSV files of hundreds of megabytes, scroll millions of rows and search them.
  Excel stops at about one million rows and text editors freeze on files of this size. This viewer opens CSV files of hundreds of megabytes in seconds: a table you can scroll through, a search across all columns and a "go to row" box. The file never leaves your computer.
  How to use: Drop a CSV file onto the page or choose it. Wait a moment while the rows are indexed (a progress bar shows the status). Scroll, jump to a row number or search; clear the search to see all rows again.
- [Restore Leading Zeros in CSV](https://ohfis.com/en/leading-zero-fixer/): Repair zip codes and IDs that lost their leading zeros in Excel.
  Excel treats 01234 as the number 1234 and silently removes the zero. Zip codes, product numbers, employee IDs and phone prefixes are damaged this way every day. This tool restores them: it detects the intended width of each column or pads to a width you choose.
  How to use: Paste the damaged CSV or open the file. Leave the width on 0 to detect it, or enter the number of digits. Pick the columns. Download the repaired file and import it with the column set to Text.
- [VLOOKUP & XLOOKUP Formula Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/vlookup-formula-generator/): Build correct lookup formulas from column letters, in English, German, French or Spanish.
  Tell the generator which cell holds the value, which column to search and which column to return, and it writes three working formulas: XLOOKUP, VLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH. Ranges are made absolute ($D$2:$D$100) so they do not drift when you fill down, and an optional IFERROR shows your own text instead of #N/A.
  How to use: Enter the cell to look up, the column to search and the column to return. Set the first and last data row, and optionally the sheet name and the text for "not found". Copy the formula you prefer into your sheet and fill it down.
- [Excel Date Serial Number Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/excel-date-converter/): Turn Excel serial numbers like 45231 into dates and dates back into serial numbers.
  Dates in Excel are stored as the number of days since a starting date, so exports and CSV files often show 45231 where you expect a date. Paste a list of serial numbers to get ISO dates (decimals become times), or paste dates to get serial numbers for formulas and imports.
  How to use: Paste serial numbers or ISO dates, one per line. Pick the date system (Windows 1900 is the default). Copy the converted values.
- [JSON to CSV Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/json-to-csv/): Flatten JSON arrays and nested objects into a CSV table for Excel.
  API responses and exports arrive as JSON, but analysts want rows and columns. Paste a JSON array of objects (or an object that contains one) and get a CSV with one row per object. Nested objects become dotted columns such as address.city, and arrays can become numbered columns, joined text or JSON text.
  How to use: Paste your JSON or open a .json file. Choose how nested arrays and objects should be flattened. Copy the CSV or download it and open it in Excel.
- [CSV to JSON Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-to-json/): Turn a CSV into JSON objects, with typed values and optional nesting.
  Turn a spreadsheet export into JSON for an API, a test fixture or a config file. The first row becomes the keys, every other row becomes an object. Numbers and true/false are converted to real JSON types, empty cells become null, and headers with dots such as address.city can be nested into objects.
  How to use: Paste your CSV or open a file. The separator is detected. Choose type conversion, nesting and formatting options. Copy the JSON or download it.
- [Transpose Table (Rows to Columns)](https://ohfis.com/en/transpose-table/): Swap rows and columns of pasted spreadsheet cells.
  Turn a wide table into a tall one, or the other way round. Paste cells from Excel or Google Sheets, or a CSV, and the rows become columns. The result uses a tab separator by default, so you can paste it straight back into a spreadsheet.
  How to use: Paste the cells or a CSV. The transposed table appears immediately. Copy it (tab separated for Excel) or download it.
- [Pivot Table Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/pivot-table-generator/): Group data and calculate sums, averages and counts without Excel.
  Summarise a long list of records into a compact table. Choose a column to group by (rows), optionally a column for the headings across (columns) and a value column; then pick sum, average, count, distinct count, minimum, maximum or median. With both rows and columns chosen you get a cross-tab with totals.
  How to use: Paste your CSV or open a file. Choose the row field, an optional column field, the value column and the calculation. Copy the pivot table or download it as CSV.
- [Split Column into Multiple Columns](https://ohfis.com/en/split-column/): Split full names, addresses or codes into separate columns by delimiter, position or pattern.
  Separate "Ann Marie Lee" into first and last name, "2024-05-06" into year, month and day, or "AB1234" into letters and digits. Pick the column, choose how to split and the tool inserts the new columns in place, naming them after the original.
  How to use: Paste your CSV and choose the column to split. Pick the split mode and enter the delimiter, positions or pattern. Copy the new table or download it.
- [Compare Two CSV Files](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-compare/): Find added, removed and changed rows and cells between two CSV files.
  Which customers were added since last month? Which prices changed? Load two versions of a table and see the differences: new rows in green, removed rows in red and changed cells in yellow with the old value crossed out. A summary counts each kind and the full report can be downloaded.
  How to use: Paste or open the original CSV on the left and the changed CSV on the right. Choose the key column that identifies a row (or compare row by row). Review the highlighted differences and download the report.
- [CSV to SQL INSERT Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-to-sql/): Turn spreadsheet rows into INSERT or UPDATE statements for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite or SQL Server.
  Paste rows from a spreadsheet and get SQL you can run: a CREATE TABLE with guessed column types, batched INSERT statements or one UPDATE per row using a key column. Quoting of table and column names follows the database you choose (backticks, double quotes or brackets).
  How to use: Paste your CSV and enter the table name. Choose the database, INSERT or UPDATE, and whether to create the table. Copy the SQL or download the .sql file.
- [Markdown Table Formatter](https://ohfis.com/en/markdown-table-formatter/): Align ragged Markdown tables into neat, readable grids.
  A Markdown table is easy to write and hard to read when the pipes do not line up. Paste your table, even one with missing outer pipes or uneven columns, and get a tidy version with every column padded to the same width. Column alignment markers (:--, :-:, --:) are preserved or can be forced.
  How to use: Paste the Markdown table. Optionally choose compact output or force an alignment. Copy the formatted table into your README or docs.
- [Excel Custom Number Format Tester](https://ohfis.com/en/excel-number-format-tester/): Try custom format codes like #,##0.00 or [>=1000]0.0,"K" on sample values.
  Custom formats in Excel are powerful and cryptic. Type a format code, paste test values and see exactly how each one will be displayed: thousands separators, decimals, percentages, scientific notation, dates and times, text, colours and up to four sections for positive, negative, zero and text values. Sixteen presets show common patterns such as accounting, K/M suffixes and leading zeros.
  How to use: Pick a preset or type your own format code. Edit the test values, one per line. Read the preview and copy the code into Format Cells → Custom.
- [CSV to GeoJSON Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-to-geojson/): Turn a list of coordinates into a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of points.
  Put a spreadsheet of places on a map. Choose the latitude and longitude columns (they are detected from names like lat, lon, latitude) and get a standard GeoJSON FeatureCollection; every other column becomes a property of the point. The result opens in geojson.io, QGIS, Mapbox, Leaflet and most GIS software.
  How to use: Paste the CSV and check the latitude and longitude columns. Review the list of skipped rows, if any. Copy or download the .geojson file.
- [Reorder & Delete CSV Columns](https://ohfis.com/en/reorder-csv-columns/): Drag columns into a new order or remove them before you share a table.
  Strip a customer export down to the columns you want to share, or put the columns in the order an import template expects. Every column becomes a card: drag it, use the arrow buttons or untick it to drop the column. A live preview shows the result.
  How to use: Paste your CSV. Drag the column cards (or use the arrows), and untick columns to delete them. Copy or download the new table.
- [Z-Score & Min-Max Normalizer](https://ohfis.com/en/zscore-normalizer/): Standardise numeric columns to z-scores or scale them to 0–1.
  Put columns with different units on the same scale before comparing or modelling them. Choose z-score (how many standard deviations from the mean), min–max scaling (0 to 1) or max-abs scaling (−1 to 1), pick the numeric columns and download the table with the new columns. The mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum of every column are shown.
  How to use: Paste your CSV and tick the numeric columns. Choose z-score, min–max or max-abs and the decimals. Copy or download the normalised table.
- [Phone Number Formatter (E.164)](https://ohfis.com/en/phone-number-formatter/): Normalise phone numbers in a list to E.164 or a readable international style.
  A contact list with (415) 555-0132, 0049 30 1234567 and +49 (0)30 1234567 cannot be imported into most CRMs and SMS tools. This tool rewrites every number in a column to E.164, the international standard (+14155550132), or to a readable international, national (US) or digits-only style, and flags the numbers it cannot read.
  How to use: Paste your CSV and choose the phone column. Pick the default country and output style. Download the cleaned list; the "valid" column shows numbers that need a look.
- [Fill Blank Cells in Spreadsheet Data](https://ohfis.com/en/fill-blank-cells/): Fill empty cells with the value above, a fixed value or the column average.
  Exports from pivot tables and reports often leave a cell empty when the value is the same as above. Models and databases do not like gaps either. Choose how to fill: the value from the cell above (fill down) or below, a fixed text, zero, or a statistic of the column such as the average, median, most frequent value, minimum or maximum.
  How to use: Paste your CSV. Choose the fill method and the columns. Copy or download the completed table.
- [Excel Formula Formatter](https://ohfis.com/en/excel-formula-formatter/): Break long nested Excel formulas into indented, readable lines.
  A formula with five nested IFs in the formula bar is nearly impossible to debug. Paste it here and get it back with one argument per line, indented by nesting level, and with spaces around operators. Short parts stay on one line. In Excel, press Alt+Enter in the formula bar to add such line breaks; they do not change the result.
  How to use: Paste the formula, with or without the leading =. Set the maximum line width and indent size. Copy the formatted formula back into the formula bar.
- [Address Parser (Split Street, City, ZIP)](https://ohfis.com/en/address-parser/): Split one-line addresses into street, number, unit, city, state and ZIP.
  Mailing lists often keep the whole address in one cell. Paste one address per line and get a table with street, house number, unit (Apt, Suite, #), city, state, ZIP and country. US addresses, UK postcodes and continental European layouts (street number, then postcode and city) are recognised.
  How to use: Paste addresses, one per line. Check the "format" column of the result. Download the table as CSV.
- [Currency to Number Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/currency-normalizer/): Turn "$1,234.56", "1.234,56 €" and "(500)" into plain numbers.
  Money in exported data arrives as text with symbols and mixed conventions: $1,234.56, 1.234,56 €, CHF 1'234.50, (500.00) or 12,5 zł. Excel cannot calculate with these. This tool converts selected columns to plain numbers with a dot as the decimal mark, and can add a column with the detected currency.
  How to use: Paste your CSV and tick the amount columns. Choose how ambiguous values like 1,234 should be read. Download the numeric table.
- [Percentage Change Calculator for Columns](https://ohfis.com/en/percentage-change-calculator/): Add a percent-change column comparing two numeric columns.
  Compare this year with last year for hundreds of rows at once. Choose the old and the new value column and the tool adds a "% change" column with the rounding you want. Growth shows as positive numbers, declines as negative ones.
  How to use: Paste your CSV. Choose the old-value and new-value columns and the number of decimals. Copy or download the table with the new column.
- [Trim Spaces in CSV & Spreadsheet Cells](https://ohfis.com/en/trim-whitespace-csv/): Strip leading, trailing and hidden spaces from every cell.
  A lookup that "should work" fails because "Berlin" and "Berlin " are different values. Paste your table and every cell is trimmed. Non-breaking spaces, which Excel's TRIM function does not remove, and invisible zero-width characters are removed too, and repeated spaces inside cells can be collapsed.
  How to use: Paste the CSV. Choose whether to collapse inner spaces and remove hidden characters. Copy or download the cleaned table.
- [CSV Header Cleaner (snake_case)](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-header-sanitizer/): Turn messy column titles into clean, database-safe names.
  Headers like "First Name", "Revenue (€)" or "2024 Sales" break imports into SQL, pandas and BI tools. This tool rewrites them as lowercase snake_case (or camelCase or kebab-case): accents are removed, symbols are spelled out (% → pct), names that start with a digit get a prefix, duplicates are numbered and SQL keywords are made safe.
  How to use: Paste the CSV with the messy header row. Choose snake_case, camelCase or kebab-case and an optional maximum length. Copy or download the table with the clean header.
- [Merge CSV Files](https://ohfis.com/en/merge-csv-files/): Combine several CSV files into one, matching columns by name.
  Twelve monthly exports, one file per branch or a folder of logs: drop them all in and download a single CSV. Files with the same columns are stacked; if the columns differ or are in a different order, they are matched by header name and missing values stay empty. An optional column records the file name of each row.
  How to use: Drop or choose two or more CSV files. Choose how to combine them and whether to add a source column. Download the merged file.
- [Sample Size Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/sample-size-calculator/): How many respondents do you need for your confidence level and margin of error?
  Before you run a survey, find out how many answers you need. Enter the confidence level (95% is standard), the margin of error (± 5 points is common) and, if the group is small, the population size. The result is the number of completed responses for a proportion estimate.
  How to use: Enter the population size (leave empty if it is very large). Choose the confidence level and margin of error. Read the required sample size and plan your survey around it.
- [CSV Encoding Fixer (UTF-8, Mojibake)](https://ohfis.com/en/csv-encoding-fixer/): Repair garbled characters like MÃ¼ller and convert files to UTF-8.
  "MÃ¼ller" instead of "Müller", "cafÃ©" instead of "café" and question marks where umlauts should be: these are encoding mix-ups. Open the file here and it is decoded with the right character set (detected automatically, or chosen from a list such as Windows-1252, ISO-8859-2 or UTF-16) and saved back as UTF-8, with a BOM if Excel needs one.
  How to use: Open the file, or paste the garbled text. Leave the encoding on automatic, or pick the one your file uses. Check the preview and download the UTF-8 file.
- [Excel Formula Translator (EN ⇄ DE, FR, ES)](https://ohfis.com/en/excel-formula-translator/): Convert formulas between English, German, French and Spanish Excel, including separators.
  A formula from an English tutorial does not work in a German Excel: it wants SUMME instead of SUM, WENN instead of IF and semicolons instead of commas. Paste the formula, pick the languages and get a version your Excel accepts. It works the other way round, too, which helps when you share files with colleagues abroad.
  How to use: Paste one formula per line. Choose the language it is written in and the language you need. Copy the translated formulas.
- [Unpivot Table (Crosstab to List)](https://ohfis.com/en/unpivot-table/): Turn a wide crosstab with one column per month into a tidy long list.
  Reports often have one column per month or year. Databases, charts and pivot tables want one row per value instead. Choose the columns that identify a row (like product or region) and every other column is turned into rows of attribute and value: Jan, Feb, Mar become a "month" column and the numbers a "amount" column.
  How to use: Paste the wide table. Tick the identifier columns and name the two new columns. Copy or download the long table.
